correctness.rationale: The exact-degree gradient and its tangent quarter-turn are orthonormal on the sphere. A latitude reflection gives the two diagonal hemisphere entries 1/2; longitude selection makes order blocks independent. Their off-diagonal integral collapses to 2πim|Y_lm(equator)|²/[l(l+1)]. The standard normalized associated-Legendre endpoint identity converts this to central-binomial factors and yields exact 2×2 eigenvalues. Ratios of adjacent positive-parity gaps are <1 as azimuthal order drops by two, and maximal gaps obey M_(l+1)/M_l=(2l+3)/(2l+4)<1, M_1=3/8. Thus all fields have 1/8≤hemisphere energy fraction≤7/8 with equality exactly in degree one and |m|=1 appropriate polarization. The checker independently recomputes associated-Legendre endpoint values and cross-integrals. The proof, not finite checks, covers all degrees.

value.rationale: The natural localization task asks how much energy a single-frequency tangential field can place in one hemisphere. Its optimal universal bound is exactly 7/8 (leakage at least 1/8), attained only in the lowest degree and an identified two-dimensional helicity subspace. Complete fixed-degree sharp constants decrease to 1/2 at an explicit rate. This is a motivated infinite classification of the optimal concentration invariant, not a test at one arbitrary mode; it remains useful despite being narrower than general cap Slepian theory.
